hypotheses: q=a/b is one of the seven locked fibers; gcd(a,b)=1; b is odd; v2(a)>=2; gcd(T,S)=1; H=U*V*A*B is a rational square.

proof: If S is odd, U and V are odd; since a is even and b odd, A and B are odd.
If S is even, primitiveness makes T odd. Writing S=2s gives v2(U)=v2(V)=1; aU and aV have valuation at least 3 while bV and bU have valuation 1, hence v2(A)=v2(B)=1.

proof_outline: If T,S are odd, v2(V)=v2(A)=1 and v2(U)>=3; square parity forces v2(U) and v2(B) to have the same parity, giving {V,A} or all four. For v2(a)=2 the {V,A} parity cannot occur because once v2(U)>3, v2(B)=3, while the equality case also cannot yield even/even parity under the square condition.

If T,S have opposite parity, U and B are odd. Square parity requires v2(V) and v2(A) to have the same parity. When v2(a)=2 this forces both even, hence no 2-squareclass. When v2(a)>=3, both-even and both-odd possibilities give none or {V,A}.
